summary: The UK Tier 1 (Investor) visa (30 June 2008 - 17 February 2022) gave residence, and settlement after 2-5 years, for GBP 1m (GBP 2m from November 2014) invested in UK bonds or companies. Home Office statistics give yearly visa grants to 2018 (peaking at 1,172 main applicants and 1,823 dependants in 2014 before the price doubled), extensions to 2024 and settlement by nationality from 2020, and the MAC 2014 report and the closure memorandum explain why it was judged of small economic value and exposed to illicit wealth. Gaps: yearly grant totals for 2019-2022 exist only as quarter-by-nationality rows, there is no official figure for money invested, and the 2023 review published only headline findings. Ireland's Immigrant Investor Programme (2012 to closure on 15 Feb 2023) is documented by archived INIS guidelines and press releases (thresholds and their changes in 2013, 2014, 2016-17), an internal 2017 evaluation and the 2020 EY reviews published in 2023, and above all ministerial answers to Dail questions, which give applications, approvals and approved investment by year (2012-2025), by option and by nationality (about 94% Chinese). There is no regular official statistics series, the yearly figures are revised between answers, and the value figures are approved, not audited, investment; persons granted residence are not counted at all. Australia: the Department of Home Affairs publishes yearly Migration Program reports (BIIP places, lodgements, pipeline, grant/refusal rates; stream tables from 2020-21) and a pivot-table workbook (BP0068) with Significant Investor grants by nationality and applicant type from 2017-18. The 2023 Review of the Migration System found poor economic outcomes for the BIIP as a whole but stronger ones for the small Significant Investor stream; the programme was frozen with the December 2023 Migration Strategy and closed to new applications in July 2024 (official sources disagree on 1 vs 31 July). There is no official measured investment total; the department's cumulative SIV figure (over AUD11.32 billion to Oct 2019) equals grants times the AUD5 million minimum.

programs.name: Tier 1 (Investor) visa (United Kingdom)
programs.notes: Residence by investment under Part 6A of the Immigration Rules (paras 245E-245EF; originally 245O-245U), created by HC 607 from 30 June 2008, replacing an 'investor' category that had existed since 1 October 1994. Investors held GBP 1m (GBP 2m from 6 Nov 2014) and invested it in UK government bonds (until 29 March 2019) or share/loan capital of UK trading companies; no job or business required. First grant 3 years 4 months, extension 2 years. Settlement (indefinite leave to remain) after 5 years, or after 3 years with GBP 5m / 2 years with GBP 10m (from 6 April 2011). Citizenship by naturalisation possible 12 months after settlement and 5 years' residence (MAC 2014: 6 years at GBP 1m, 5 years at GBP 5m/10m). Closed to new applicants at 16:00 on 17 Feb 2022 by CP 632; existing investors could extend until 17 Feb 2026 and may apply to settle until 17 Feb 2028. Home Office statistics count visas per person and separate main applicants from dependants; no official figure for total money invested.

programs.name: Immigrant Investor Programme (IIP)
programs.notes: Residence by investment run by the Department of Justice (INIS, later Immigration Service Delivery) under a Government decision of 2012 and ministerial guidelines, without its own legislation. Approved investors and their spouse/partner and minor children got Stamp 4 residence (right to work and study): 2 years, renewed for 3, then 5-year renewals while the investment (held at least 3 years) stayed in place. No residence obligation beyond visiting Ireland once a year. No fast track to citizenship: naturalisation needs 5 years' physical (reckonable) residence, so investors who did not live in Ireland could not qualify. Projects were vetted by an inter-departmental Evaluation Committee; the minister decided. Most money went via the enterprise option into project vehicles (nursing homes, social housing, hotels) put together by agents for groups of mainly Chinese investors. Closed to new applications 15 Feb 2023; applications on hand and investors for already approved projects are still being processed (1,192 pending in March 2026).

programs.name: Business Innovation and Investment Program (BIIP): Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa subclass 188, (Permanent) subclass 888, Business Talent subclass 132
programs.notes: Umbrella programme for business and investor migrants under the Migration Regulations 1994. Provisional (subclass 188, four years; five years from July 2021) then permanent residence (888) if conditions are met; Australian citizenship can follow after the usual residence requirement for permanent residents. Streams over time: Business Innovation, Investor (AUD1.5m bonds 2012-2021; AUD2.5m complying investment 2021-2024), Significant Investor (see aus-siv), Premium Investor (2015-2021, AUD15m, not researched here), Entrepreneur, Business Talent, Venture Capital Entrepreneur. Most applicants needed state/territory nomination. Closed to new applications in July 2024 (1 July per the 2024-25 Migration Program report, 31 July per the visa website); on-hand applications still processed. Programme numbers are Migration Program places, primary and secondary applicants together.

programs.name: Significant Investor visa (SIV): Significant Investor stream of the Business Innovation and Investment visa (subclass 188C provisional, 888C permanent)
programs.notes: A stream within aus-biip, kept as its own programme because it is the "golden visa" part. AUD5 million complying investment held for the provisional visa (four years; five from July 2021), with Complying Investment Framework rules from 1 July 2015 and revised ratios from 1 July 2021. No points test; nomination by a state/territory government or Austrade. For permanent residence (888) the investor had to spend 40 days a year in Australia, or the spouse 180 days. Permanent residents can later apply for citizenship under the normal residence rules. 2,264 primary SIVs were granted to 31 Oct 2019; most applicants were Chinese nationals. Closed to new applications 31 July 2024.
